rules.text: The Japanese people forever renounce war as a sovereign right of the nation and the threat or use of force as means of settling international disputes.
Land, sea, and air forces, as well as other war potential, will never be maintained, and the right of belligerency of the state will not be recognized.
All the people shall be respected as individuals, and their right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness shall be the supreme consideration in legislation and in other government affairs.
All people are equal under the law and shall not be discriminated against for political, economic or social relations or by race, creed, sex, social status or family origin.
The people have the inalienable right to choose their public officials and to dismiss them.
No person shall be held to involuntary servitude of any kind, except as punishment for a crime.
Freedom of thought and conscience shall not be infringed.
No person shall be compelled to participate in, maintain, support or finance any religious institution.
No person shall be restrained in his right to keep and carry arms, to assemble peaceably without arms, or to associate.
All people shall have the right to freedom of choice of their residence and occupation, and of leaving Japan and giving up their nationality.
Academic freedom shall be inviolable.

Marriage shall be based upon the mutual consent of both sexes and shall be ensured through the equal rights of husband and wife with emphasis on individual dignity and the essential equality of the sexes.
All people shall have the right to receive an equal educational opportunity in accordance with the principles laid down by law.
All people have the right and the duty to work.
The rights of workers to organize, to bargain collectively and to take collective action are guaranteed.
Property rights shall be inviolable, and the details concerning property rights shall be determined by law.
The people shall be liable, according to law, to be taxed for public purposes.
No person shall be arrested or detained except upon a specific charge stated and by due process of law.
No person shall be denied the right of access to the courts.
No person shall be apprehended or detained except upon a warrant issued by a competent judicial officer specifically indicating the ground therefor.
In all criminal cases, the accused shall be provided promptly with an itemized specification of the charges against him, and shall have the right to confront the witnesses against him.
The inviolability of the rights of all people to be free from unreasonable searches and seizures shall be secured.
No person shall be tortured or subjected to cruel punishment.
In all criminal cases, the accused shall be provided promptly with an itemized specification of the charges against him, and shall have the right to confront the witnesses against him.
No person shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

ministries.name: National Diet
ministries.mandate: Legislative authority is vested in a bicameral National Diet.

ministries.name: House of Representatives
ministries.mandate: The lower house of the National Diet with the final authority to nominate the Prime Minister and override the House of Councillors' veto on any bill.

ministries.name: House of Councillors
ministries.mandate: The upper house of the National Diet.

ministries.name: Cabinet
ministries.mandate: Executive authority is vested in a cabinet, jointly responsible to the Diet, and headed by a Prime Minister.

ministries.name: Supreme Court
ministries.mandate: The highest body of the judiciary with the power of judicial review.

ministries.name: Emperor
ministries.mandate: The symbol of the State and of the unity of the people, exercising only a ceremonial role.

fields.value: {"id": "15", "text": "The people have the inalienable right to choose their public officials and to dismiss them.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Democratic elections: Article 15 provides that "the people have the inalienable right to choose their public officials and to dismiss them". It guarantees universal adult (in Japan, persons age 20 and older) suffrage and the secret ballot.

fields.value: {"id": "18", "text": "No person shall be held to involuntary servitude of any kind, except as punishment for a crime.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Prohibition of slavery: Guaranteed by Article 18. Involuntary servitude is permitted only as punishment for a crime.

fields.value: {"id": "19", "text": "Freedom of thought and conscience shall not be infringed.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Freedom of thought and conscience (Article 19)

fields.value: {"id": "20", "text": "No person shall be compelled to participate in, maintain, support or finance any religious institution.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Separation of Religion and State: The state is prohibited from granting privileges or political authority to a religion, or conducting religious education (Article 20).

fields.value: {"id": "21", "text": "No person shall be restrained in his right to keep and carry arms, to assemble peaceably without arms, or to associate.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Freedom of assembly, association, speech, and secrecy of communications: All guaranteed without qualification by Article 21, which forbids censorship.

fields.value: {"id": "22", "text": "All people shall have the right to freedom of choice of their residence and occupation, and of leaving Japan and giving up their nationality.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Rights to change residence, choose employment, move abroad and relinquish nationality (Article 22)

fields.value: {"id": "23", "text": "Academic freedom shall be inviolable.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Academic freedom (Article 23)

fields.value: {"id": "24", "text": "Marriage shall be based upon the mutual consent of both sexes and shall be ensured through the equal rights of husband and wife with emphasis on individual dignity and the essential equality of the sexes.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Equality between the sexes is explicitly guaranteed in relation to marriage (Article 24) and childhood education (Article 26).

fields.value: {"id": "26", "text": "All people shall have the right to receive an equal educational opportunity in accordance with the principles laid down by law.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Compulsory education (Article 26)

fields.value: {"id": "27", "text": "All people have the right and the duty to work.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Workers' rights: Work is declared both a right and obligation by Article 27 which also states that "standards for wages, hours, rest and other working conditions shall be fixed by law" and that children shall not be exploited.

fields.value: {"id": "28", "text": "The rights of workers to organize, to bargain collectively and to take collective action are guaranteed.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Workers have the right to participate in a trade union (Article 28).

fields.value: {"id": "29", "text": "Property rights shall be inviolable, and the details concerning property rights shall be determined by law.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Right to property: Guaranteed subject to the "public welfare". The state may take property for public use if it pays just compensation (Article 29).

fields.value: {"id": "30", "text": "The people shall be liable, according to law, to be taxed for public purposes.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: The state also has the right to levy taxes (Article 30).

citations.source_text: Right to due process: Article 31 provides that no one may be punished "except according to procedure established by law".

citations.source_text: Protection against unlawful detention: Article 33 provides that no one may be apprehended without an arrest warrant, save where caught in flagrante delicto.

fields.value: {"id": "34", "text": "In all criminal cases, the accused shall be provided promptly with an itemized specification of the charges against him, and shall have the right to confront the witnesses against him.", "applies_to": "all"}

citations.source_text: Article 34 guarantees habeas corpus, right to counsel, and right to be informed of charges.

citations.source_text: Protection against entries, search and seizures (Article 35)

citations.source_text: Prohibition of torture and cruel punishments (Article 36)

citations.source_text: Right to a fair trial: Article 37 guarantees the right to a public trial before an impartial tribunal with counsel for one's defence and compulsory access to witnesses.

fields.value: {"name": "National Diet", "mandate": "Legislative authority is vested in a bicameral National Diet.", "has_veto": false, "veto_scope": "", "vote_weight": 1}

citations.source_text: The constitution provides for a parliamentary system and three branches of government, with the National Diet (legislative), Cabinet led by a Prime Minister (executive), and Supreme Court (judicial) as the highest bodies of power.

fields.value: {"name": "House of Representatives", "mandate": "The lower house of the National Diet with the final authority to nominate the Prime Minister and override the House of Councillors' veto on any bill.", "has_veto": false, "veto_scope": "", "vote_weight": 1}

citations.source_text: The House of Representatives has the sole ability to pass a vote of no confidence in the Cabinet, can override the House of Councillors’ veto on any bill, and has priority in determining the national budget, and approving treaties.

fields.value: {"name": "House of Councillors", "mandate": "The upper house of the National Diet.", "has_veto": true, "veto_scope": "Any bill", "vote_weight": 1}

citations.source_text: The new constitution provides that both chambers be directly elected, with a lower House of Representatives and an upper House of Councillors.

citations.source_text: The judiciary consists of several lower courts headed by a Supreme Court.

citations.source_text: In contrast with the Meiji Constitution, the Emperor’s role is entirely ceremonial, as he does not have even nominal powers related to government.
